purpose: Create a compile-ready private theory/model first draft that separates definitions, design choices, proof obligations, open hypotheses, planned simulations, and actual results.
audience: Network science, computational social science, security, and scientific-peer-review researchers; internal authors before venue selection.
section_type: full theory/model manuscript with a deliberately empty results section
outline: Heterogeneous actors and transitive trust boundaries
Preregistered experiments, observables, and no-go rules
Results evidence gate and bounded discussion
evidence_packets: bounded primary-source web retrieval performed 2026-08-24; identities recorded in verification artifacts
bibliography_inputs: primary publisher, conference, institutional, or canonical author pages only
human_questions: Which author list and corresponding author should be used?
Which target venue should control length and style after analytical results exist?
What exclusion ceiling for newcomers and qualified minorities is scientifically acceptable?
Which restricted/HPC workflow may be used for later resource calibration?
constraints: Private draft; no publication or external contact
No simulation or empirical result described as completed
Every absent result is protected by an evidence gate
Prior-art components are credited rather than claimed as inventions
Graph scores and review votes are never equated with scientific validity
excluded_claims: The bridge bound has been proved
The mean-field model has a demonstrated phase transition
Fresh personas provide a deployed privacy guarantee
The framework generalizes beyond scientific review
